text.p: Value Health Inc said Friday that a ruling from a Massachusetts court will temporarily delay consummation of its merger with Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp.

The court granted a preliminary injunction at the request of FHC Options Inc, which claimed that its partnership with a Value Health subsidiary to provide mental health services to Medicaid beneficiaries would have been hurt by the merger.

Value Health said the partnership has submitted a revised plan to the State of Massachusetts to eliminate any conflict of interest and is in talks with the Division of Medical Assistance about the plan.

"We anticipate the transaction will close as soon as the preliminary injunction granted today is lifted and certain regulatory matters concerning the State of California Department of Corporations are resolved," Value Health said in a statement Friday evening.

In a separate release, Columbia/HCA said the merger would close as soon as the injunction is lifted and as soon as "regulatory issues with the State of California Department of Corporations are resolved."
It did not elaborate on the regulatory issues that needed to be resolved, and phone calls to both companies seeking further information were not immediately returned.
Value Health said in its release that it expects to return to court early next week with new information.

The companies announced in January plans to merge in a stock swap deal valued then at $1.3 billion. In April they revised their plan to give stock holders of Value Health $20.50 in cash for each share in a deal valued at $1.2 billion.
The deal, which was approved Value Health shareholders last week, was scheduled to be completed in the second quarter.
Value Health shares closed down 1/4 Friday at 19-7/8.
Those of Columbia/HCA closed up 5/8 at 39-1/2.
